SeabedNet · CHS NONNA archive, completed by model · Sept 2026

Churchill Corridor Atlas

Canada is investing $262.5M to reopen the Churchill trade corridor. Under its 2,327 km shipping route, only 17% of the seabed has ever been surveyed — and full Arctic charting is officially “more than a decade” away. This atlas completes the rest by model: depth and uncertainty for every kilometre, with the provenance of every pixel kept honest.

Exhibit A — the corridor, found

The channel no one drew — computed from depth and uncertainty

Given only the completed seabed and its σ field, the model traced the least-risk channel from Churchill to the Atlantic itself: 2,782 km, never shallower than 22 m, mean σ of 2.7 m — and not one kilometre over unanswered water. Where the straight route crosses red, the found channel goes around.

Cyan: the computed channel. Dashed grey: the straight-line route. Cost per km = distance × (shallow-water penalty + σ/8 + no-data ×13); water under 20 m and land impassable.
Exhibit B — provenance

The corridor, completed — and honest about which pixel is which

82,121 km² surveyed → +351,305 km² completed, every inferred pixel within 6 km of a real sounding. Blue is measured; amber is model. No pixel pretends to be the other.
Exhibit C — uncertainty

Where the corridor is still uncertain

The insurers’ map. Bright veins are the highest-σ water — and the route threads straight through them in the Hudson Strait approaches. Uncertainty, not ice, is what limits the shipping season; this is the first map of exactly where it lives.
Exhibit D — the stakes

Tasmania Islands, Franklin Strait — September 6, 2025

The MV Thamesborg, an ice-class freighter bound from China to Baie-Comeau, struck what the Transportation Safety Board calls an “uncharted shoal” (case M25C0241) at the western tip of the Tasmania Islands. Salvage took a month and an icebreaker. In July 2026 the Dutch Maritime Disciplinary Court suspended the Master’s licence for deliberately routing through a zone whose survey reliability was rated CATZOC C — poorly surveyed water — when a better-charted lane lay further west. 75% of this water had no depth data at all. The right panel is the same water, completed.

The chart was blank here. The model’s map wasn’t. In the left panel you can see the surveyed lane passing west of the islands — the route the court said the ship should have taken. Grounding position from AIS/press reports (TSB has not published coordinates).
Exhibit E — the plan

Where a survey ship earns its day rate first

The σ map, converted to procurement: the ten highest-uncertainty boxes within 35 km of the route, priced in ship-days at the public icebreaker rate of C$205,000/day.

Total: ~219 ship-days, C$44.9M to de-risk the worst water on the route — a fundable season, against “more than a decade” for full conventional coverage.

Exhibit F — the completed product

Not just the corridor. Canada.

The same model, run over the entire national archive: all 437 NONNA blocks — three oceans and the Great Lakes. 429,682 km² of surveyed seabed extended by +1,088,182 km² of completed seafloor, every pixel carrying its own σ. This is the asset the corridor exhibits are cut from.

Every charted Canadian water, completed. Blue: the CHS archive. Amber: SeabedNet v5, within 6 km of soundings.
And the national uncertainty field — the survey-priority map for the whole country, the same way Exhibit E prices the corridor.
Method & the honest numbers

What we claim, and what we don’t

10.53 m

Held-out error, geographic holdouts

SeabedNet v5 mean absolute error on three fully held-out regions of real surveyed seabed — against 11.37 m for the best physics baseline on identical patches.

+48%

Better than physics near soundings

Within 500 m of any sounding, v5 error is 7.2 m vs 14.3 m for gravity-derived bathymetry. The advantage decays with distance and reaches parity beyond ~1 km.

0.63

Uncertainty that ranks correctly

Per-pixel σ correlates 0.63 with actual error — valid for ranking where to survey, stated as uncalibrated in absolute terms.

≤ 6 km

Provenance discipline

Inference is only published within 6 km of a real sounding. The stated physics baseline itself ingests historical ship soundings, so far-from-data comparisons favour it unfairly on surveyed test areas — we say so rather than hide it.

PLANNING PRIOR — NOT FOR NAVIGATION

Data: Canadian Hydrographic Service NONNA-100, Open Government Licence — Canada. Gravity prior: SRTM15+ (Scripps). Model: SeabedNet v5 (34.8M-parameter masked-completion network, gravity-anchored, resolution-conditioned), trained and validated on geographic holdouts. Corridor completion: 94 blocks, Hudson Bay · Hudson Strait · Labrador approaches · Franklin Strait.

Public record cited: Churchill Plus investment (C$262.5M, 2026); CCGS icebreaker day-rate (≈C$205k); CHS statement on Arctic charting timelines; TSB Canada investigation M25C0241 (“uncharted shoal”, open); Dutch Maritime Disciplinary Court ruling, July 2026 (CATZOC C finding, officer suspensions); grounding position from AIS and press reporting — Nunatsiaq News, gCaptain, Maritime Executive, SWZ|Maritime.
